newsitem.title: USA: Local officials voice concern on U.S. budget bills.
newsitem.headline: Local officials voice concern on U.S. budget bills.

text.p: A trade group representing state and local officials sent letters to House and Senate finance committees on Monday urging lawmakers to adjust several provisions in the proposed fiscal 1998 budget.

The Government Finance Officers Association, which represents 13,500 state and local officials, sent letters detailing GFOA's position on extending the de minimus rule, arbitrage rebate relief for schools, and a permanent moratorium from pension non-discrimination rules for pension plans.
The House bill includes a provision that would deny nonfinancial corporations a deduction on interest earned from tax-exempt bonds, the so-called de minimus rule.
The effect of the provision, which is not included in the Senate bill, would be to decrease corporate demand for tax-exempt securities, GFOA said in urging lawmakers to oppose the idea.

On the Senate side, the budget proposal contains a provision to raise the small-issuer arbitrage rebate exception annual issuance limit to $10 million from $5 million. The House bill does not include the provision.
GFOA urged support for the idea, which it said would reduce compliance costs for issuers of school bonds.

Finally, the letter said state and local governments are "especially pleased" that both the House and Senate bills contain provisions that would make permanent the 20-year moratorium from federal pension nondiscrimination rules for public pension plans.

"These rules were designed to identify discriminatory practices in the private sector and are not appropriate for the public sector," the letter said, adding that public plans are already covered by strict state and local oversight.
